subject: community-medicine
title: History of Medicine and Public Health: Key Milestones and Primary Health Care

steps.tx: Hippocrates is called the **Father of Medicine** and is credited as the first true epidemiologist because he linked disease with environment, climate and water. His book Air, Water and Places is a classic exam reference. Galen later described predisposing, exciting and environmental causes of disease.
steps.say: Hippocrates is called the Father of Medicine and is credited as the first true epidemiologist, because he linked disease with environment, climate and water. steps.tx: John Snow showed in 1854 that contaminated drinking water spread **cholera** in Soho, London. He used a **spot map** of deaths around the Broad Street pump to find the source. This is a classic natural experiment, and his work is the basis of modern epidemiology.
steps.say: John Snow showed in 1854 that contaminated drinking water spread cholera in Soho, London. He used a spot map of deaths around the Broad Street pump to find the source. This is a classic natural experiment, and his work is the basis of modern epidemiology.

steps.tx: Pasteur disproved **spontaneous generation** and proposed the **germ theory of disease**. Koch gave postulates to link a specific microbe to a disease, and showed that bacteria cause anthrax. Jenner developed the **smallpox vaccine** in 1796 and coined the term vaccine.

steps.tx: Edwin Chadwick led the **sanitary awakening** in Britain, stressing clean water and sewage removal. William Farr is called the father of modern epidemiological surveillance. Joseph Lister introduced antisepsis, and Ronald Ross worked out the life cycle of plasmodium in mosquitoes.
